summary: Bagot Bluff (Pointe-Sud) light on Anticosti Island: an 1870 wooden tower, the 1912 concrete tower with flying buttresses, and keepers from 1871. Automated 1963.

access.note: LighthouseFriends: owned by the Canadian Coast Guard; grounds open, tower closed; best seen by boat, with a distant view possible from island roads; walking in is not advised because the ground is marshy. The federal register notes that listing does not make a site open to the public.

notes_for_editor: 1) Station identity: LighthouseFriends calls the station Escarpement Bagot (South Point) and places it at Pointe-Sud on the south-east coast; the Quebec register and Les amis call it the phare de l'escarpement Bagot. The 1906 and 1913 Department lists name 'Anticosti South Point' and 'Bagot bluff', each with keeper Emile Laprise. Those two lines were matched by OCR column position, so the link between the names rests on the keeper and on LighthouseFriends. The federal register (record 10890) places the 1870s tower on the island's east point, not South Point. 2) Coordinates: the record's position (49.066 N, 62.260 W) matches LighthouseFriends (49.065972, -62.259778). The federal register gives 49.391 N, 63.595 W for the Bagot Bluff designation. That is roughly 100 km apart by my estimate. Check which point is the lighthouse before editing the record's location. 3) First light: 1870 (LighthouseFriends, Quebec register) against 1871 (Les amis); the record says 1871. Editor to decide. 4) Heights: the record's tower of 15.7 m is the skeletal tower (LighthouseFriends about 15 m); the 24.3 m concrete tower is missing from the record's structures. Focal height: the record gives 17.2 m; LighthouseFriends gives 19.5 m for the skeletal tower. 5) The concrete tower's date: 1912 (federal register, LighthouseFriends, Les amis) against 'vers 1906-12' (Quebec register). The story gives both. 6) Ownership, agency and visiting arrangements: LighthouseFriends says the Canadian Coast Guard owns the lighthouse, the grounds are open and the tower closed, and that it is best seen by boat (used in the story's Today section). The Parks Canada register pages returned only their wrapper to the reader, so no register states ownership. The record's Canadian Coast Guard agency is therefore supported by LighthouseFriends only. 7) Recent keepers: LighthouseFriends names keepers up to 1963. They are named only in their keeping role, with no personal detail. 8) The Renommee (1736) rests on LighthouseFriends alone, which names no source; kept in the story with that said. 9) The 1870 contract quotation is as LighthouseFriends quotes the 1870 Department report; that report is not in the corpus (marine_ca begins 1900). 10) The Quebec register text has an OCR typo ('bçati'); quotes are copied from the cached page as printed. 11) Les amis des phares is a non-profit site; used for dates and height only. 12) LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: the story paraphrases it, with short quotations only in the evidence. 13) Position checks on the page image (2026-10-27): the 1913 'Bagot bluff' row with E. Laprise was viewed on scan p. 72 (printed p. 65), and the station and the keeper share one printed row. The 1906 'Anticosti South Point' line (scan p. 338) was not legible at the viewer's resolution, so its keeper pairing rests on the same-line OCR and on the 1909 and 1910 reports, which print 'Anticosti, south point' with Emile Laprise on one line. 14) The 1901 Menier passage concerns West Point (scan p. 56); the South Point, Heath Point and Southwest Point statement is attributed in the story to Menier's surveyor, as the report gives it.
